papers.title: Venomics AI: a computational exploration of global venoms for antibiotic discovery
A generative artificial intelligence approach for peptide antibiotic optimization.

metrics.usage: Proportion of predicted peptides showing antimicrobial activity in vitro
metrics.evidence: 53 out of 58 synthesized VEPs (91.4%) exhibited activity against at least one pathogenic strain.

metrics.usage: Percentage of ApexGO-optimized peptides with enhanced antimicrobial activity against Gram-negative pathogens
metrics.evidence: ApexGO achieved an 85% ground-truth experimental hit rate and a 72% success rate in enhancing antimicrobial activity against Gram-negative pathogens.

important_evidence: APEX predicted 386 unique venom-encrypted peptides with high activity, 58 synthesized, 53 active (91.4% hit rate).
ApexGO optimized 100 peptides, 85% ground-truth hit rate, 72% success in enhancing activity against Gram-negative pathogens.
DBAASP database contained 19,762 known AMPs; venom proteins sourced from ConoServer, ArachnoServer, ISOB, VenomZone.
uncertainties: Code and trained weights for APEX and ApexGO are not publicly available in the provided evidence.
Training data for APEX (in-house peptides) is not publicly described, preventing reproducibility.
ApexGO's VAE training data details are missing, and the exact peptide sequence dataset used is not specified.
The exact URL for DBAASP database was not provided in the evidence.
